strings.book.death_notice.text:
ROYAL BUREAU OF RECORDS — DISTRICT OF BELLWETHER

Notice of Administrative Decease:
Be it known that the bearer of this writ expired seventeen (17) winters past. All chattels were auctioned to cover municipal interment fees. Remaining balance due: 142 crowns in unpaid burial tax.

If you wish to contest your deceased status, report immediately to Clerk Oakhaven at the Bellwether Registry Office and submit Form 27-B.
strings.book.form_27b.text:
FORM 27-B: APPLICATION FOR TEMPORARY EXEMPTION FROM BEING DEAD

Section I: Applicant certifies under penalty of perjury that they are currently breathing, corporeal, and occupying no more than one (1) point in history.
Section II: Attach corroborating ledger entry from Annex III.

[Stamped in glowing pale ink: APPROVED BY ARCHIVIST MORVATH BEFORE THE GREAT SILENCE]
strings.book.uncounted_ledger.text:
THE UNCOUNTED LEDGER — FOLIO IX

"We did not erase the seven cities out of malice. When the flaw in the world's foundation widened, every name spoken aloud gave the Hunger another door. We struck their names from the Grand Register so the dark could not find them.

Yet the ink is fading. Today a traveler walked into Bellwether seventeen years after we hid their name to save their life. Worse still: the final page records that Bellwether itself will be uncounted at the next new moon unless the seal is renewed."
strings.book.tome_ember.text: On the Ignition of Aether: Speak the syllable of cinder and project the spark outward.
strings.book.tome_mend.text: Litany of the Dawn: Recall the body's unblemished pattern from yesterday's ledger.
strings.book.tome_ward.text: Treatise on Abjuration: Fold ambient stone-memory into a shield before the blow lands.
strings.book.tome_glimmer.text: Cantrip of the Archivist: A steady light that neither smokes nor scorches vellum.
strings.book.tome_veil.text: Notes on Un-Noticing: Step between the lines of the observer's attention.

strings.quest.legally_deceased.title: Legally Deceased
strings.quest.legally_deceased.summary: The Royal Bureau of Records insists you died seventeen years ago. Clear your name—or uncover why it was erased.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage0: Speak with Clerk Oakhaven inside the Bellwether Records Office.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal0: I arrived in Bellwether carrying a formal notice declaring that I died seventeen years ago and owe burial taxes. I should confront the local records clerk.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage10: Travel east along the Old Road to the abandoned Registry Annex and retrieve Form 27-B.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal10: Clerk Oakhaven informed me that I am legally dead and cannot file a correction without Form 27-B from the old Registry Annex east of town. He handed me the brass key to the Annex door.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage20: Explore the Registry Annex & Forgotten Crypt to find Form 27-B and the truth behind the altered records.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal20: Kaelen of the Ashbound warned me that the Registry Annex has physically shifted—its lower vaults now open into a pre-Silence crypt where names were deliberately erased.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage30: Return to Clerk Oakhaven in Bellwether with Form 27-B and The Uncounted Ledger.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal30: Deep beneath the Annex, I defeated the Archivist Shade and recovered both Form 27-B and The Uncounted Ledger—which reveals that names were erased to hide people from an ancient catastrophe, and Bellwether is next.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage100: Chapter Zero Complete: You entrusted the Uncounted Ledger to the Royal Bureau.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal100: I surrendered the Uncounted Ledger to Clerk Oakhaven. My legal existence is restored, and the Bureau has quietly dispatched riders to the capital—though I wonder whether they intend to repair the seal or bury the truth.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage101: Chapter Zero Complete: You kept the Uncounted Ledger for the Ashbound.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal101: I forced Clerk Oakhaven to stamp Form 27-B while keeping the Uncounted Ledger out of the Bureau's hands. I am legally alive again, and I hold the key to the Great Silence.
strings.dlg.clerk.greeting: "Name? ...Ah. Deceased. Seventeen years ago, third column from the bottom. Terribly sorry. If you're here to pay your burial arrears, the coffer is on the left."
strings.dlg.clerk.explain_27b: "Yes, and that's highly irregular. You'll need Form 27-B: Application for Temporary Exemption from Being Dead. Three copies, please. Unfortunately, our last stack was stored in the Old Registry Annex down the eastern road before the floorboards started humming. Take this brass key and fetch a copy yourself."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_persuade_fee: [Persuasion] "If I'm retrieving Bureau property from a hazardous ruin, I'm entitled to a courier stipend."
strings.dlg.clerk.persuade_stipend: Oakhaven blinks behind his spectacles, consults a subsection of the municipal code, and sighs. "Sub-clause 14: Perilous Retrieval by a Non-Living Contractor. Very well. Thirty-five crowns in advance. Try not to die a second time; the paperwork is dreadful."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_where_annex: "Remind me where the Registry Annex is."
strings.dlg.clerk.annex_directions: "Follow the cobbles east out of Bellwether onto the Old Road. Pass the ruined watch-arch and you'll find the Annex door set into the hillside."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_race_dwarf: [Dwarf] "My clan's stone-rolls don't misplace a living person by seventeen years, clerk."
strings.dlg.clerk.dwarf_remark: "With respect to the mountain vaults, master dwarf, parchment is much more accommodating when history changes its mind."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_race_elf: [Elf] "This ink smells of Silence-era abjuration, not clerical error."
strings.dlg.clerk.elf_remark: Oakhaven lowers his voice. "Then you understand why I don't go down into the Annex cellar myself."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_have_proof: "I have Form 27-B—and this Uncounted Ledger from the vault beneath the Annex."
strings.dlg.clerk.inspect_ledger: Oakhaven's ink-stained fingers tremble as he reads the stone-vellum pages. "Merciful dawn... these entries are dated next month. It says the Great Silence wasn't an attack—it was an emergency erasure to keep something locked away, and the seal under Bellwether is failing. Give me that Ledger at once so I can seal it in the Royal Vault!"
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_surrender_ledger: "Take the Ledger. The Bureau has the resources to warn the realm."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_keep_ledger: "No. Stamp my Form 27-B, Oakhaven, and I'll take the Ledger to those who won't bury the truth."
strings.dlg.clerk.ending_bureau: Oakhaven stamps Form 27-B with a resounding thud and locks the Ledger inside his iron safe. "You are officially alive, citizen. Take this compensation from the Bureau treasury. When the High Chroniclers read this... Edrath will never be the same."
strings.dlg.clerk.ending_independent: Oakhaven swallows hard, stamps your Form 27-B three times, and steps back. "Legally, you exist again. Off the record? Run. If the Ledger is right, the road beyond Bellwether is waking up."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_back: "Let's return to the matter at hand."
strings.dlg.merchant.greeting: "Welcome to Bellwether Provisions! Whether you're legally alive, administratively misplaced, or somewhere in between, your gold spends the same."
strings.dlg.merchant.choice_rumors: "Heard anything strange along the Old Road?"
strings.dlg.merchant.rumors: "Caravan guards swear there used to be a whole toll-village two leagues east called Oakhallow. Last week the road-sign went blank, and now nobody can remember who lived there—except my ledger still shows they owe me for twelve barrels of salt."
strings.dlg.marta.greeting: "Come in out of the damp, traveler. The fire's warm, even if half the town is pretending the sky doesn't look wrong at dusk."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_remember_me: "Do you remember me, Marta? The Bureau claims I died seventeen years ago."
strings.dlg.marta.remember_witness: Marta stares at you closely, rubbing her temples. "I... I remember pouring ale for your father when you were a child—no, wait. Half the memory feels like pages torn out of a book. Something in that Annex down the Old Road is eating our yesterdays."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_rest: "Could I rest by the hearth a moment?"
strings.dlg.marta.rested: "There now. Warm soup and a dry cloak do wonders for the living."
strings.dlg.fenwick.greeting: "Shh! Keep your voice down! And if you see a translucent gentleman shelving books in the history aisle, do NOT engage him."
strings.dlg.fenwick.ghost_fees: "Certainly not! Hauntings require municipal certification. Those apparitions are merely delinquent patrons who expired before paying their late fees—and until they settle three centuries of overdue fines, I refuse to acknowledge them!"
strings.dlg.fenwick.choice_train_magic: "Can you teach me anything of Collegium magic?"
strings.dlg.fenwick.train_magic: "A fellow seeker of illumination! Take this Glimmer primer and remember: light reveals what the ledgers try to hide."
strings.dlg.aldous.greeting: "May the Last Dawn keep your name written in the sun's memory, traveler."
strings.dlg.aldous.choice_silence: "What does the Church teach about the Great Silence?"
strings.dlg.aldous.great_silence: "That the gods drew a curtain of mercy across a broken world. Though between you and me... curtains are meant to keep something out, not merely hide the view."
strings.dlg.aldous.choice_blessing: "I could use a blessing for the road ahead."
strings.dlg.aldous.blessed: Aldous traces a warm golden circle above your brow. Your wounds ache less.
strings.dlg.scout.greeting: "Halt—ah, steady. You don't move like one of those bone-rattlers from the ruin. I'm Kaelen of the Ashbound."
strings.dlg.scout.choice_annex: "I'm heading into the Registry Annex for Form 27-B."
strings.dlg.scout.annex_warning: "Watch your footing inside. The upper offices collapsed into an older pre-Silence vault. Look for an iron wall-lever in the eastern archive to raise the crypt portcullis—and check the cracked northern wall if you have keen eyes."
strings.dlg.scout.choice_orc_kinship: [Orc] "Good to see another of the marches out here, Kaelen."
strings.dlg.scout.orc_gift: "Blood and stone, cousin! Take these healing draughts. Don't let the Bureau clerks write your story for you."
strings.dlg.spirit.greeting: "...Are you real? Or another line of ink waiting to be scraped from the vellum?"
strings.dlg.spirit.choice_who: "Who are you? What happened in this vault?"
strings.dlg.spirit.explain_prison: "I was an Archivist when the Great Silence fell. We built the Uncounted Vaults to hide living souls from the Unmaking—but Chief Archivist Morvath bound himself to the Ledger and went mad guarding it. Take this Cold-Iron Key. Open the northern sanctum, defeat Morvath's shade, and read the Ledger before Bellwether is erased next!"
strings.map.edrath.name: The Borderlands of Edrath
strings.story.prologue.1:
Edrath, in the four hundred and twelfth year after the Great Silence.

The kingdoms keep their ledgers carefully now. What is written down, exists. What is struck out was never there at all.
strings.story.prologue.2:
Seventeen years ago, by order of the Royal Bureau of Records, you died.

You do not remember it. Nobody does. That is rather the point of a ledger.
strings.story.prologue.3: This morning a notice arrived anyway, sealed in Bureau wax: proof of your death, and a bill for your burial.
strings.story.prologue.4: So you have walked to Bellwether, where the rain never quite stops, to argue with a clerk about whether you are alive.
strings.ui.prologue.continue: Click or press E to continue
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.title: A Name Worth Keeping
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.summary: Someone scratched a question onto Oakhallow's boundary stone: why do they remember a baker's daughter from a town that no longer exists?
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.stage0: Ask Marta at the Lantern Inn about Oakhallow and its baker's daughter.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.journal0: Oakhallow's boundary stone claims 412 souls lived where the forest now stands. Beneath the carving, fresh charcoal: "Why do I remember the baker's daughter?" Marta bakes Bellwether's bread. If anyone remembers a baker, it might be her.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.stage10: Search the Registry Annex's archive for any record of Oakhallow's baker and his daughter.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.journal10: Marta's hands knew the Oakhallow braid before her mind did. She remembers a girl with flour on her nose who taught her to fold the dough, but not the girl's name, nor any town called Oakhallow. If the Bureau ever wrote the child down, the record is in the Annex.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.stage20: The girl was Ilse Brannock. Ask the Uncounted Witness in the crypt what "moved to Vault III" means.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.journal20: A struck census folio names the baker's household: Tomas Brannock and his daughter Ilse, aged nine, "moved to Vault III for safekeeping." The spirit in the crypt calls itself a remnant of Annex III.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.stage30: Return to Bellwether and speak Ilse Brannock's name to Marta.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.journal30: The Witness says the Archivists hid the children first: names into the Ledger, bodies into sleep, memories out of every mind that loved them. A name held truly by someone who remembers cannot be unmade. Marta still dreams of Ilse.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.journal100: I said the name aloud in the Lantern Inn and Marta's face changed like a window opening. Ilse was her little sister. Marta was from Oakhallow too; the Bureau took her town and her family and left her a bread recipe she couldn't explain. She is baking the braid again tonight. She says it's for someone who's coming home.
strings.dlg.marta.choice_oakhallow: "Do you know anything about a town called Oakhallow? Or a baker's daughter?"
strings.dlg.marta.oakhallow:
Marta's hands stop moving in the dough. "Oakhallow... no. Never heard of it." She looks down. Her fingers have folded the loaf into a tight four-strand braid without her noticing. "That's odd. A girl taught me this. Flour on her nose, laughing at my clumsy knots. I can see her plain as day. I can't for the life of me tell you her name."

She wipes her hands slowly. "If the Bureau ever wrote her down, it'll be in those vaults under the Annex. Find her for me?"
strings.dlg.marta.choice_ilse: "Marta... the baker's daughter. Her name was Ilse. Ilse Brannock."
strings.dlg.marta.ilse:
For a long moment Marta doesn't breathe. Then she laughs, and the laugh breaks halfway into something else.

"Ilse. Little Ilse. She was my sister. We grew up above our father's ovens in Oakhallow. Seventeen years I've been baking her braid and I couldn't remember why."

She presses a warm loaf and a pouch of coins into your hands. "Don't argue. Somebody gave me back my family today. Bread is the least I can do."
strings.dlg.spirit.choice_ilse: "Do you know what became of a girl named Ilse Brannock? Her record says 'moved to Vault III'."
strings.dlg.spirit.ilse:
The spirit flickers like a candle in a draught. "Vault III. The children's vault. We hid them first. Their names went into the Ledger, their bodies into a long sleep, their memories out of every mind that loved them. That was the price: the Hunger cannot find what no one remembers."

"But a name held truly by someone who remembers cannot be unmade. If anyone still dreams of her, say her name to them. Say it aloud."
strings.bark.marta.1: Mind the puddles. The rain's been falling sideways since the new moon.
strings.bark.marta.2: Odd. I keep setting out one more bowl than I have guests.
strings.bark.marta.3: Bread's nearly done. Smells like winter mornings somewhere I've never been.
strings.bark.marta.ilse: I've baked the braid for her again. Silly, isn't it? It's good to be silly.
strings.bark.vaelen.1: Potions, arrows, lockpicks! Everything a dead person needs!
strings.bark.vaelen.2: The Bureau taxes the living and the dead alike. Guess which pays more reliably.
strings.bark.vaelen.3: Heading east? Buy two of everything. Nobody comes back from the Annex with change.
strings.bark.fenwick.2: The history aisle is closed. For... reshelving. Indefinitely.
strings.bark.fenwick.3: Three centuries of overdue fines. I will collect. Eventually.
strings.bark.aldous.1: The sun remembers what we forget.
strings.bark.aldous.2: Pray for the uncounted, friend. Even if you cannot remember who they were.
strings.bark.clerk.1: Form 88-A is for vanished spouses. Form 27-B is for vanished selves.
strings.bark.clerk.2: Next! ...Ah. The deceased. Still upright, I see.
strings.bark.clerk.3: Have you retrieved the form? The Bureau does not accept 'I was busy being dead'.
strings.bark.scout.1: Hear that? The road hums at night. Like a choir with no mouths.
strings.bark.scout.2: Every stone out here was somebody's doorstep once.
strings.bark.scout.3: Back from the dark, and still yourself? Good. Keep it that way.
strings.bark.spirit.1: Say my name... no. I have forgotten it too.
strings.bark.spirit.2: The ink is cold down here. It remembers everything we tried not to.
strings.line.sentinel.alert: HALT. YOUR NAME IS NOT ON THE LIST.
strings.line.keeper.alert: A name walks in my halls. I will strike it from the page!
strings.line.keeper.death: The ink... is running. Forgive me, little ones...
strings.ending.ilse: In the Lantern Inn, Marta now bakes an Oakhallow braid every morning and sets it by the window. She says it is for someone who is coming home.
strings.map.vault_three.name: Vault III: The Nursery
strings.quest.vault_three.title: The Sleepers of Vault III
strings.quest.vault_three.summary: Beneath the crypt, the Archivists hid the children of erased towns in an enchanted sleep. Something down there is still keeping them.
strings.quest.vault_three.stage0: Follow the floury handprints down into Vault III.
strings.quest.vault_three.journal0: In the crypt, a child's handprints in old flour lead to a gap in the west wall and a stair going down, deeper than the Annex was ever built.
strings.quest.vault_three.stage10: The hidden children sleep in the Nursery. Find what keeps them asleep: descend to the Seal Chamber.
strings.quest.vault_three.journal10: I found Ilse Brannock asleep beneath clouded glass, nine years old for seventeen years, whispering her sister's name. Rows of small sarcophagi line the Nursery. A hymnal speaks of a Seal that someone must sign before morning can come.
strings.quest.vault_three.stage100: Completed: you signed the Seal of Names.
strings.quest.vault_three.journal100: The Lullaby Warden sang its last verse and fell silent. I signed the Seal of Names with my own name, the one the Bureau struck out seventeen years ago, and the ink held. The sleepers are safe a while longer, and Bellwether will not be uncounted at the new moon. The rain over the village has stopped.
strings.story.seal.1:
The quill is cold, and the ink beneath it is older than the Bureau, older than Edrath's kings.

The Seal asks only one thing: a name, written by its owner, freely given.
strings.story.seal.2:
You write the name the Bureau struck out seventeen years ago. Your own.

For a moment the ink does not take. Then, letter by letter, it soaks into the vellum like rain into dry ground.
strings.story.seal.3: All around the chamber, the old runes on the monoliths brighten, then settle to a steady glow. Somewhere above, in the Nursery, forty small chests rise and fall a little easier.
strings.story.seal.4: And far above the Annex, above the Old Road, the rain over Bellwether stops for the first time in seventeen years.
strings.flour.handprints.title: Handprints in Old Flour
strings.item.seal_quill.name: Archivist's Seal-Quill
strings.item.seal_quill.desc: A raven quill with a nib of black iron, still wet with ink that never dries. It wrote the Seal of Names. Worn at the belt, it steadies the mind. +2 Will, +2 Intellect.
strings.enemy.lullaby_warden.name: The Lullaby Warden
strings.line.warden.alert: Hush now. Hush. It isn't morning yet.
strings.line.warden.death: Who will... sing them... to sleep...
strings.ending.seal: Beneath the Annex, the Seal of Names holds, signed in your own hand. The rain has stopped over Bellwether, and at the next new moon the village is still on every map.
strings.map.seal_chamber.name: The Seal Chamber
strings.dlg.marta.choice_sleeper: "Beneath the Annex, there's a girl asleep under glass. Flour on her hands. She looked like you."
strings.dlg.marta.sleeper_unnamed:
Marta sets the bread knife down very carefully, as if it might break.

"Asleep. Under the ground." She presses a floury palm flat against her chest. "That's a cruel story to tell a baker, traveler. Why does it hurt like it's mine?"

She shakes her head. "If she has a name, find it. I can't. I've tried."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_ilse_alive: "Marta, there's more. Ilse isn't dead. I found her asleep in a vault beneath the Annex."
strings.dlg.marta.ilse_alive:
Marta grips the edge of the counter. "Asleep." Her voice is very small. "Seventeen years, and she's still nine?"

You tell her about the Nursery: the clouded glass, the rows of little sarcophagi, the girl whispering her sister's name.

"Then something down there is keeping her." Marta wipes her eyes with the back of her wrist and leaves a streak of flour. "Whatever it is, you go back down and you make it stop singing. Please. I'll keep the hearth lit."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_ilse_alive_safe: "Marta, Ilse isn't dead. She's asleep beneath the Annex, and she's safe now. I signed the Seal that keeps them."
strings.dlg.marta.ilse_alive_safe:
Marta sits down on the flour sacks as if her knees have simply quit.

"Asleep. Safe." She looks toward the window, at the dry street and the first clean sky Bellwether has seen in seventeen years. "That's why the rain stopped, isn't it? You did that."

She takes your hand in both of hers. They are warm and smell of yeast. "When she wakes she'll want breakfast. She always wanted breakfast. I'll be ready."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_seal_signed: "I went back down, Marta. The Warden is silent and the Seal is signed. Ilse is safe."
strings.dlg.marta.seal_signed:
Marta closes her eyes and listens: no rain on the shutters, only the fire. "I heard it stop. I was kneading and the whole house went quiet, and I knew."

She presses a warm loaf into your arms, wrapped in a cloth embroidered with an oak leaf. "Oakhallow's mark. I didn't know I could sew it until this morning."
strings.bark.marta.dry: No rain. I keep going to the window to make sure.
strings.bark.marta.alive: Every morning I set the braid by the window. Every morning is one closer.
strings.dlg.clerk.rain_stopped:
"Yes. I noticed." Oakhaven straightens a stack of forms that is already straight. "I've filed it under Irregularities, Meteorological. Then something else happened, and I have no form for it."

He opens the great register of the dead and turns it toward you. Your entry has faded to the colour of weak tea. Beneath it, in a neat hand that is not his, forty new lines have appeared overnight, all children, all marked Oakhallow, all marked not deceased.

"Whoever you are," he says quietly, "I think the Bureau owes you an apology. I'm not authorised to issue one. Consider this... unofficial."
strings.bark.clerk.dry: Forty new entries overnight, and none of them in my handwriting. Most irregular.
strings.bark.clerk.puddles: My inkwell has been watered down by the leak for seventeen years. Today it isn't. I don't trust it.
strings.ending.ilse_alive: She tells everyone who asks that her sister is only sleeping, and for once in Bellwether nobody argues with a record.
